newsitem.title: INDIA: India will attract foreign investment - Deve Gowda.
newsitem.headline: India will attract foreign investment - Deve Gowda.

text.p: Indian Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda reiterated on Thursday that the government would soon take steps to attract more private domestic and foreign investment.

Deve Gowda told the annual meeting of the Confederation of Indian Industry in the eastern city of Calcutta that he had assured industrialists at a meeting on December 31 that the government would "attract the domestic as well as global investments by simplifying all the procedures".
Deve Gowda said there were certain "bottlenecks" in private investment.
"We will see that the further climate of more investment will be created," Deve Gowda said.
At the December meeting with industrialists in New Delhi, Deve Gowda had promised to announce measures by mid-January to strengthen capital markets.
"We are simplifying the procedures in various aspects. I think in the next 15 days, further steps will be taken," he said without elaborating.
